__attribute__((noreturn)) in function pointer argument applies to function's type
<!-- Thanks for filing a bindgen issue! We appreciate it :-) -->

### Input C/C++ Header

```c
void foo(__attribute__((noreturn)) void (*arg)(void));
```

### Bindgen Invocation

`$ bindgen /tmp/foo.h`

### Actual Results

```rust
/* automatically generated by rust-bindgen 0.66.1 */

extern "C" {
    pub fn foo(arg: ::std::option::Option<unsafe extern "C" fn() -> !>) -> !;
}
```

### Expected Results

```rust
/* automatically generated by rust-bindgen 0.66.1 */

extern "C" {
    pub fn foo(arg: ::std::option::Option<unsafe extern "C" fn() -> !>);
}
```

Note the lack of the second `-> !`.

### Notes

I'm fairly sure the problem is here:

[HIDDEN]

### Additional contract requirements

- When `__attribute__((noreturn))` is attached only to a function-pointer parameter, the generated pointer type must be diverging (`-> !`), but the containing function must not be marked as diverging and must return normally. An independent `noreturn` attribute on the containing function still makes it diverging.
